title: Bench setup
summary: Review instrument readiness, result sources and material lots before analytical work.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: The Instruments tab shows service status and result-source registrations. Open an instrument to inspect its readiness and use the source actions offered for your role. For result-file instruments, the template actions lead to drafting or checking a file template.

The Lots tab lists laboratory materials. Authorized quality staff can register a lot and use the available lot actions. Runs record the lots used rather than relying only on what is currently listed here.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Keep connection settings and readiness decisions distinct. Instruments in Laboratory setup configures how data arrives; Bench setup records whether the instrument and its sources are ready for work.

Check the actual material identity and expiry details when registering a lot. Approve a source only after the laboratory’s required comparison and review. Source approval does not itself approve the results that arrive through it.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: Read the service, source or lot status associated with a blocked run. An enabled connection can still lack an approved source or acceptable readiness. Configuration and quality actions require the corresponding authority; ask the responsible person to resolve the specific status shown.

pages.title: Bench setup: Instruments and Lots
pages.purpose: Review service readiness and result sources, and register the materials used at the bench.
pages.access: Any signed-in account can read instrument readiness, lots and source registrations. Setting service status and managing lots requires quality-management authority. Registering sources requires configuration-management authority; approving requires configuration-approval authority.

fields.name: Tabs
fields.meaning: Selects the readiness list.
fields.values: Instruments or Lots.
fields.rules: Defaults to Instruments.

fields.name: Instruments: Instrument / Service status / Status since
fields.meaning: Identifies the instrument and latest readiness decision.
fields.values: Configured name; In service, Out of service or Status not recorded; decision time when known.
fields.rules: Read-only; no recorded status is not ready for a run.

fields.name: Approved result source
fields.meaning: Identifies the source currently used to interpret this instrument’s data.
fields.values: Sender/software name and version, or None approved.
fields.rules: Read-only; supplied by the current record.

fields.name: Set status: Status
fields.meaning: Records current readiness.
fields.values: In service or Out of service.
fields.rules: Required; no default.

fields.name: Set status / Withdraw lot: Reason
fields.meaning: Explains the quality decision.
fields.values: Free text.
fields.rules: Required, trimmed 1–1,000 characters; retained in the audit history.

fields.name: Register source: Sender name
fields.meaning: Matches the sender named in the analyzer message header. AU400 / AU640 messages carry no sender name, so for an AU analyzer it is the device identity the laboratory declares.
fields.values: Exact source identity supplied by the analyzer; for AU, the declared analyzer model, such as AU640.
fields.rules: Required, trimmed 1–200 characters. Confirm against the actual source.

fields.name: Register source: Sender version
fields.meaning: Identifies the source software version. For an AU analyzer it is the declared software version, since AU messages carry none.
fields.values: Version text supplied by the analyzer, or declared for AU.
fields.rules: Required, trimmed 1–200 characters.

fields.name: Sample ID is read from
fields.meaning: Chooses which analyzer identifier carries the container label.
fields.values: Specimen ID field or Instrument specimen ID field.
fields.rules: Required; no default. Not asked for an AU analyzer: an AU source always matches the sample ID of the AU message to the container barcode, shown as a fact in the dialog.

fields.name: Corrected results
fields.meaning: Declares how this source identifies corrections.
fields.values: The analyzer does not mark corrections; Corrections carry a corrected result status.
fields.rules: Required; must describe the actual source behavior. Not asked for an AU analyzer: an AU source is always recorded as The analyzer does not mark corrections.

fields.name: Reports final concentration after dilution
fields.meaning: Declares whether numeric values already incorporate dilution.
fields.values: Yes or No.
fields.rules: Required; no default. The application does not apply a numeric dilution correction for you.

fields.name: Test codes: Source test code
fields.meaning: Maps an analyzer test identifier to the catalog.
fields.values: Exact source code; for AU, the analyzer's two-digit test number, 01–99.
fields.rules: At least one mapping required. Each code is 1–64 characters, unique, and must have no surrounding spaces. For AU, the form refuses anything but two digits from 01 to 99 before sending. Map only numeric AU assays; leave out LIH (serum index) tests, which stay held.

fields.name: Test codes: Analyte
fields.meaning: Chooses the analyte reported by that source code.
fields.values: Configured catalog analytes, by name and code.
fields.rules: Required for every test-code row.

fields.name: Test codes: Unit (AU only)
fields.meaning: Declares the unit of that numeric AU assay. AU messages carry no units, so imported values take this declared unit; result evidence still shows that no unit was reported.
fields.values: Unit text as the laboratory declares it, such as ng/mL; empty declares a unitless assay.
fields.rules: Optional; at most 64 characters, no surrounding spaces. Shown only for AU analyzers. Approved with the source; check it against the assay's actual reporting unit.

fields.name: AU wire settings (AU only)
fields.meaning: Shows the AU framing and format settings the source restates from the analyzer's connection.
fields.values: Transmission class, start and end codes, BCC, sample ID width and result width, from Laboratory setup › Instruments.
fields.rules: Read-only; copied when the dialog opens. They must still equal the connection when the source is approved, so a connection change in between blocks approval; register a new source then.

fields.name: Result sources: State / Registered / Approved
fields.meaning: Shows source version lifecycle and who authored and approved it.
fields.values: Draft, awaiting approval; Active; Retired; recorded times, each person shown by the person's current account display name.
fields.rules: Read-only. Approval activates a draft and retires the previous active source.

fields.name: Result sources: Sample ID read from / Corrections / AU wire settings / Reports final concentration / Test codes
fields.meaning: Shows the stored mapping and source declarations, so the approver sees exactly what approval activates.
fields.values: Recorded choices and source-code → analyte mappings. An AU source also shows its wire settings and each code's declared unit, or no unit for a unitless assay.
fields.rules: Read-only; file sources show their result-file shape and open in the template workspace.

fields.name: Lots: Show
fields.meaning: Controls whether unusable materials are hidden.
fields.values: Active lots; All lots, with withdrawn and expired.
fields.rules: Defaults to Active lots.

fields.name: Material
fields.meaning: Classifies the material being registered.
fields.values: Reagent, Calibrator, Control, Internal standard.
fields.rules: Required; no default.

fields.name: Product
fields.meaning: Identifies the product from its packaging.
fields.values: Free text.
fields.rules: Required, trimmed 1–200 characters.

fields.name: Lot number
fields.meaning: Identifies the manufacturer’s lot.
fields.values: Text copied from packaging.
fields.rules: Required, trimmed 1–64 characters; material kind, product and lot number must not duplicate an existing lot.

fields.name: Level
fields.meaning: Names the level used for comparison.
fields.values: Lab/manufacturer text such as Level 1.
fields.rules: Optional, trimmed, at most 64 characters; no acceptance range is inferred.

fields.name: Sample label
fields.meaning: Identifies the control/calibrator label sent by the analyzer.
fields.values: Exact label text.
fields.rules: Required for Control and Calibrator, despite the form not marking it required; 1–64 characters. Leave blank for Reagent and Internal standard.

fields.name: Expires on / Expires
fields.meaning: Records the stated expiry date.
fields.values: Valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
fields.rules: Required; expired lots cannot be used for new analytical work.

fields.name: Lot Status / Registered
fields.meaning: Shows eligibility and registration time.
fields.values: Active, Expired or Withdrawn; recorded date/time.
fields.rules: Read-only; withdrawal takes precedence in the display. Runs retain historical lot associations.

fields.name: Source approval: Confirm self-approval
fields.meaning: Records an explicit acknowledgment when the source author approves their own draft.
fields.values: I confirm that no second person reviewed this.
fields.rules: Appears only when the laboratory separation-of-duties policy permits self-approval and requests confirmation; initially unchecked. It does not override a requirement for another approver.

actions.name: Open instrument or lot row
actions.does: Shows the record’s facts and actions.
actions.result: Opens a panel with Previous, Next and Close.

actions.name: Set status
actions.does: Records a service status and reason.
actions.result: Adds an attributed readiness event; subsequent work checks this state.

actions.name: Register source
actions.does: Records the analyzer’s source declarations and mappings as a draft.
actions.availableWhen: Configuration-management authority on an applicable analyzer.
actions.result: Creates a source awaiting approval; data is not imported under the draft.

actions.name: Add test code / Remove
actions.does: Adds or removes an unsaved code-to-analyte row.
actions.result: Changes the draft form; at least one valid mapping is needed to register.

actions.name: Approve source
actions.does: Activates the displayed draft source after confirmation.
actions.availableWhen: Configuration-approval authority and the separation-of-duties rule permit approval.
actions.result: Retires the earlier active source; applies the new mapping to subsequent import work.

actions.name: New file template
actions.availableWhen: Configuration-management authority and a result-file instrument.
actions.result: Creates no source until Save draft is submitted there.

actions.name: Check and approve / Open template
actions.does: Opens an existing file source for inspection and sample checks.
actions.availableWhen: A file source is listed; Check and approve is offered when approval is allowed.

actions.name: Register lot
actions.result: Shows the newly registered lot; does not attach it to an existing run.

actions.name: Withdraw lot
actions.availableWhen: Quality-management authority and lot is still active.
actions.result: Prevents future use; prior run associations remain.

restrictions: Service readiness does not configure serial, network or watched-folder connections; those are in Laboratory setup.
Source approval does not approve patient results. Self-approval is possible only when the laboratory separation-of-duties policy allows it and the author explicitly confirms it.
An AU source cannot have its own wire settings: they come from the analyzer's connection, which is changed only in Laboratory setup › Instruments.
There is no lot-edit or restore-withdrawn-lot action here. Record material identity accurately before registration.
workflow: Open the instrument and confirm its service state and active source.
If updating a source, register or draft it, verify the mapping, and have an authorized approver activate it.
In Lots, register the actual materials from their packaging. Use All lots to investigate a withdrawn or expired record.

troubleshooting.problem: A control or calibrator cannot be registered.
troubleshooting.recovery: Enter its exact Sample label and confirm the material kind; the engine requires that label.

troubleshooting.problem: The author cannot approve a source.
troubleshooting.recovery: Use an authorized independent approver, or follow an already approved laboratory policy that permits and explicitly confirms self-approval.

troubleshooting.problem: Registering or approving an AU source says the source format must match the instrument connection and its exact AU wire settings.
troubleshooting.recovery: The analyzer's connection changed after the dialog opened or after registration. Close the dialog, reopen Bench setup and register the source again so it restates the current settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Register source says the AU tests must match the source analyte map.
troubleshooting.recovery: Each test-code row is one numeric AU test; remove duplicate codes and any LIH test, then register again.
Choose All lots to check expiry or withdrawal; register the actual replacement material rather than reusing its identity.
